A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Atlas Gaussians work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ShapeNet generation results, Objaverse text-conditioned generation results, and VAE ablations in Tables 1-4 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports expanded Objaverse comparisons, additional ablations, diversity and controllability analyses, and image-conditioned generation examples.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds an image-conditioned variant by replacing the CLIP text encoder with a CLIP image encoder and training the latent diffusion model accordingly. The core Atlas representation, patch decoder, VAE losses, and EDM procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: ShapeNet unconditional generation and Objaverse text-conditioned generation remain. Appendix B and Figure 9 add a limited real-image-conditioned generation task, illustrated with two inputs. The enlarged Objaverse sample does not by itself establish additional dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: GVGEN joins the Objaverse comparisons in Table 2 and Figure 6 alongside retained LN3Diff, LGM, and Shap-E. The ShapeNet comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged. GVGEN was already cited in v1, but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: The stated Objaverse training subset increases from approximately 6K to 18K shapes. v2 adds FID/KID evaluation using 250 prompts and 24 rendered views per object, and reports using an updated LN3Diff model trained with more data. Appendix A also changes ShapeNet Chair's latent dimension d0 from 64 to 4; this reported setting revision does not establish that the unchanged Table 1 results were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 expands fixed-patch Gaussian-count scaling into a joint patch-count/Gaussian-count analysis with memory measurements. Table 4 adds an attribute-decoding ablation. New Figure 7 examines sampling diversity, prompt control, and training-set nearest neighbors. Appendix A.2 additionally reports sensitivity to halving or doubling the rendering-loss weight.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly identifies Figure 7's diversity examples as generations using different random seeds, adding qualitative sampling-seed information. Neither version reports quantitative repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces CLIP scores, including ours changing from 30.08 to 30.66, adds FID/KID results, and changes our inference time from 3.5 to 4 seconds. Table 3 replaces the PSNR/time presentation with expanded LPIPS/memory results and revised LPIPS values. Table 4 adds a 26.55 PSNR decoding variant, and new qualitative results appear. Table 1's numbers remain unchanged. Changed Objaverse settings prevent interpreting the revised scores as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The representation definitions, interpolation equations, training losses, and attention-complexity reasoning are retained. The EDM equations move from Section 3.3 to Appendix A.3 with renumbering. No substantive mathematical revision or new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: scalable and theoretically unlimited Gaussian decoding, an efficient transformer decoder, integration into VAE plus latent diffusion, and superior generation performance. The shortened title and more precise feature-disentanglement wording do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies that shared latents prevent independently sampling geometry and appearance, interprets the attribute-decoding ablation, and explains patch overlap and the patch-versus-Gaussian efficiency tradeoff. It drops the earlier discussion of dependence on 3D training data and future training on in-the-wild images. The geometry-extraction limitation is retained in Appendix C.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds dataset-filtering information, approximately six days of Objaverse VAE training, CLIP text conditioning, 10% conditioning dropout, and guidance scale 3.5. Appendix B documents background removal for image conditioning. These extend the already detailed hardware, optimizer, architecture, and training disclosures; the added guidance description alone does not establish a changed text-generation method.

R1.justification: v2 adds the CLAY citation and removes the Perceiver IO reference and explicit architectural attribution. It also develops a direct comparison with previously cited GVGEN. The broader positioning relative to AtlasNet, implicit representations, and feed-forward versus optimization-based generation remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, polishes wording, and changes citation style. It condenses Section 3.3 by moving EDM details into Appendix A.3, subdivides the implementation appendix, relocates retained limitations, and removes the broader-impacts paragraph. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 becomes a much larger five-method comparison, Figure 5 replaces examples and adds artifact annotations, and Table 3 is redesigned as a patch/Gaussian-count grid. The earlier appendix montage is expanded and revised as Figure 8; Figures 7 and 9 are new analyses and image-conditioned examples. These accompany a document-wide template and layout change.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more informative support for the method through the GVGEN comparison, additional distributional metrics, controlled scaling and decoding ablations, and clearer conditioning documentation. These gains are tempered by the unexplained Chair latent-setting revision with unchanged scores and an error in Section 4.4: it describes 0.1-0.2 LPIPS improvements where Table 3 shows 0.001-0.002. The net improvement is useful but limited by these reporting weaknesses.
